**Stable, published under the npm `latest` dist-tag.** A plain
`npm install @candid-core/schema` selects this version once it is published;
`beta` stays on 0.3.0-beta.1. Until 1.0, any release may change the builder
API, the inferred domain types, the codec's wire behaviour, and the codes and
`$`-rooted paths validation reports. Pin an exact version.

`@candid-core/schema` 0.3 breaks the 0.2 API (principal values are canonical text, collapsing opts are boxed, every `vec nat8` is a `Uint8Array`, generated modules use a new binding layout and may omit declarations, and the `./actor`, `./transport-icp`, `./forms` and `./labels` subpaths are gone); there is no compatibility layer.

## Installation

```sh
npm install --save-exact @candid-core/schema@0.3.0
```

The generator that emits modules for this release is `@candid-core/cli`
0.2.0, which declares this package as an optional peer at exactly `0.3.0`:

```sh
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @candid-core/cli@0.2.0
```

## Pairing

- **`candid-core`**: pairs with `0.1.0-beta.3` (crates.io). Every Contract
  document `candid-core` 0.1.0-beta.3 writes loads in this release, so the
  README's `cargo install candid-core --version 0.1.0-beta.3` then
  `candid-core compile --envelope` on-ramp produces documents this release
  loads. That includes a document holding a type on a cycle through `opt`
  alone, which 0.1.0-beta.3 still compiles: it loads, and decoding a
  non-`opt` value at it ends in a `value_depth` refusal. No crate release is
  needed first. The repository's `candid-core` source has four changes over
  that archive: a leading UTF-8 byte order mark accepted (#176); a run of
  more than 256 consecutive comments refused (#219); a type on a cycle
  through `opt` alone refused by the compiler (#234); and a struct written
  as a JSON array refused by the Contract loaders (#235). The first widens
  what compiles, the next two narrow it, and the last narrows what the Rust
  loaders read to the object form candid-core has always written. None moves
  a Contract or an identity of an input both 0.1.0-beta.3 and this source
  accept. This package's own loader changed for none of the four: it already
  refused the array form.
- **Generator**: the `candid-core-ts` generator is unpublishable on crates.io;
  it reaches consumers only inside `@candid-core/cli`. The generator revision
  this release pairs with is the one `@candid-core/cli` 0.2.0 embeds: the
  commit both packages are dispatched from, recorded in each run.
- **Lockstep**: the CLI peers this exact version, and is published right
  after it.

## Public API against 0.2.0

The previous stable release. Exported names of the shipped `dist/*.d.ts`,
0.2.0 (rebuilt from its `gitHead`, `956f2a198cb89fe40d273ac67089ae15e2095f7a`;
the rebuilt tarball's SHA-512 integrity equals the registry's,
`sha512-ypBHMbB05ORQ6c0I…`) against this release, with the comment-stripped
declaration text of every kept name compared. Every break is marked
**BREAKING** and is in the changelog, under 0.3.0 or 0.3.0-beta.1.

Export map: `.`, `./validate`, `./contract`, `./codec` remain.

| Subpath | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `./actor` | **BREAKING**, removed: `createActor`, `callFunc`, `ActorError`, `Transport`, `CallTarget`, `ActorOptions` |
| `./transport-icp` | **BREAKING**, removed: `httpTransport`, `HttpTransportOptions` |
| `./forms` | **BREAKING**, no longer exported: `formModel`, `formNodeAt`, `FormNode`, `FormCommon`, `FormArm`, `FormControl` |
| `./labels` | **BREAKING**, no longer exported (still shipped as an internal module): `candidLabelHash`, `numericKeyId`, `isNumericShapedName`, `fieldIdOfKey`, `utf8BytesStrict`, `utf8Decode` |
| `peerDependencies` | **BREAKING**, the optional `@icp-sdk/core >= 6` peer is dropped; no dependency of any kind remains |

| Entry | Name | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.` | `PrincipalValue` | **BREAKING**, removed |
| `.` | `Principal` | added: branded canonical text |
| `.` | `principal` | added: the one conversion point |
| `.` | `isPrincipal` | added |
| `.` | `OptDomain` | added |
| `.` | `isBoxedOpt` | added |
| `.` | `c` | **BREAKING**, `c.principal` is `PrimitiveSchema<Principal>` |
| `.` | `FuncValue` | **BREAKING**, `principal` is `Principal` |
| `.` | `ServiceSchema` | **BREAKING**, extends `Schema<Principal>` |
| `.` | `OptSchema` | **BREAKING**, extends `Schema<OptDomain<T>>` (collapsing opts boxed) |
| `./validate` | `ResourceLimitInfo` | **BREAKING**, `resource` gains `"stack"` |
| `./codec` | `DecodedPrincipal` | **BREAKING**, removed |
| `./codec` | `CodecResourceLimitInfo` | **BREAKING**, `resource` gains `"stack"` |
| `./codec` | `principalTextFromBytes`, `principalBytesFromText` | unchanged signatures, now re-exported from an internal module |
| `./contract` | `ContractIssueCode` | **BREAKING**, loses `"unrepresentable_option"` and gains `"unknown_key"`, `"orphan_type_node"` and `"rootless_type_arena"` (17 members) |

Kept with identical declaration text: 20 of the 24 kept names of `.`, 13 of
14 in `./validate`, 10 of 12 in `./contract`, and 14 of 17 in `./codec`.
Shipped but not exported: the internal modules `labels`, `options`,
`principal-text` and `typetable`, whose deep imports the packaged-consumer
gate refuses.

Against 0.3.0-beta.1 (rebuilt from its `gitHead`,
`a65d7e204135ef80a4802f07f1153bbefe913d8f`; integrity equal to the
registry's, `sha512-fO7uDzR1Dv8vvLec…`) the only declaration change is
`ContractIssueCode`'s three new members. The `rec` hop change (#231) moved
documentation comments in `schema.d.ts`, `validate.d.ts` and `codec.d.ts`
and no declaration.

Behaviour breaks beyond the declaration changes above — strict principal
validation and encoding, `TypeError` on unknown or invalid options, the
structural type table, the loader's blob rule and omissions, the loader
refusing unknown keys, unreachable type nodes and a rootless arena, and the
three narrow input refusals of the `rec` hop change below — are in the
changelog, each marked **BREAKING**.

## Resource limits: a `rec` hop is no longer charged

`validate`, `encode` (in its value walk) and `decode` no longer charge a
`rec` hop against `maxDepth` or `maxElements` (#231). Before, a value of a
Contract-loaded schema, recursive or not, reached `maxDepth` at about 128
levels and `maxElements` at about 500,000 elements, half of candid-core's
`max_value_depth` and `max_value_elements`. Now a value is charged for its
constructors alone, so a generated, a Contract-loaded and a `c`-built
schema of one type give the same verdict, whenever `maxDepth` is at least
the schema's longest hop chain: as deep (256) as candid-core's
`validate_host_value` under its defaults, and as wide (1,000,000) except
that `validate` and `encode` also count each examined record or variant
key (#241, below).

Inputs now refused that were accepted before, each marked **BREAKING
(input)** in the changelog:

- **A tag-only variant at exactly `maxDepth`.** The `null` payload of
  `{ tag }` is now checked one level below its variant in `validate` and
  `encode`, as `decode` and candid-core already checked it. So a value whose
  tag-only variant sits at exactly a caller-set `maxDepth`, with no `rec` on
  the path from the root to it, is refused: `c.vec(c.variant({ a: c.null }))`
  holding `[{ tag: "a" }]` at `maxDepth: 1` gives `value_depth`, observed 2.
  A generated module writes method argument and result types inline, so this
  is not only hand-built. At the default `maxDepth` of 256 no
  compiler-accepted type reaches it.
- **A field the wire omits is charged at its own level.** `decode` now
  charges the `null` it supplies for an omitted `opt`, `null` or `reserved`
  field (or trailing argument) one depth check at the field's own level and
  one element, as it charges the same `null` read from the wire. So a record
  at exactly `maxDepth` whose message omits such a field is refused
  (`value_depth` at the field's path), and so is a message whose omitted
  fields take it past `maxElements` (`value_elements`; a `vec record {}` of
  500,000 elements read at `vec record { x : opt nat }` now costs 1,000,001).
  `validate` refuses the same value under the same limits, and every value
  `decode` returns at a `maxDepth` is one `validate` accepts at it.
- **An omitted required field behind an omitted `opt` field.** A missing
  required field is still charged nothing, so an enclosing `opt` absorbs it,
  unless the record also omits an `opt`-like field earlier in field-id order
  whose `null` already crosses a limit. That `null` is now refused where the
  enclosing `opt` used to decode as `null`: `record {}` read at
  `opt record { a : opt nat; b : nat }` with `maxDepth: 1` is now
  `value_depth` at `$.a`. With the two fields in the other id order it
  still decodes to `null`.

Two trade-offs, documented in the changelog and the JSDoc:

- **The hop-chain cap is `maxDepth`.** More than `maxDepth` consecutive hops
  resolving one reference are refused with `value_depth`, which is how a
  mis-built `c.rec(() => self)` terminates. A caller-set `maxDepth` below a
  schema's longest chain therefore refuses a value where it reaches that
  chain, even one the same type built with no `rec` accepts: at
  `maxDepth: 0`, `c.rec(() => c.nat)` refuses `1n`. A generated module needs
  one or two hops, a Contract-loaded schema one. That was so before as well.
- **Chain resolution is uncharged work, bounded by `maxDepth` hops per
  resolution**, not by `maxElements`. Generated and Contract-loaded schemas
  pay a few thunk calls per constructor. A hand-built schema with long chains
  multiplies the work per constructor by their length, and with a raised
  `maxDepth` a self-referential chain costs `maxDepth` thunk calls in
  `validate` and `decode` before it is refused, where the element charge
  used to stop it at `maxElements`.

## Known limitations and deferred work

- No compatibility layer for the 0.2 API, by decision (#197).
- The Rust-reference differential fuzz of the TypeScript runtime (#196)
  runs a committed corpus in CI and holds every known divergence by case and
  issue. Those it found ship as follows:
  - a Contract document without a `declarations` key is refused, which
    `Contract::from_json` accepts (#228); the refusal is kept by decision:
    candid-core always writes the key;
  - declarations whose records canonicalize to one node share its field
    names, so a declaration can get another's spelling: a named spelling
    beats a numeric one in any order (a field written `100` loads as `d`,
    whose hash is 100, when another declaration spells it so), and of two
    names with one hash the one the provenance sidecar lists last wins
    (#229); documented and deferred by decision, because the fix changes the
    Contract format;
  - a type on a cycle that passes only through `opt` (`type T = opt T`) has
    no verdict: decoding a value that is not an `opt` at it unwraps `opt`
    without end. candid-core's compiler, and so `candid-core-cli gen`, now
    refuses such a type (#234). A Contract that already holds one, written
    by hand or by `candid-core` 0.1.0-beta.3, still loads here and in
    `Contract::from_json`, and decoding at it still ends in a `value_depth`
    refusal.
- Two divergences from candid-core, found while fixing those, are open owner
  calls and ship as today's behaviour: `validate` (and `encode`'s value
  walk) charge each examined record or variant key against `maxElements`,
  which candid-core's `validate_host_value` does not, so a record-shaped value
  reaches the element bound before candid-core's, and a value `decode`
  returns can need a larger `maxElements` in `validate` (#241); and
  `Contract::from_json` accepts serde's map form of a unit variant
  (`"primitive": {"nat": null}` for `"primitive": "nat"`), which
  `schemaFromContract` refuses (#238).
- Refusing `Infinity` as a limit may be revisited before 1.0 (#190).
- NaN payload bits are not preserved by the `number` domain (#178).
- Two structurally equal record declarations still collapse to the first
  name in generated modules (#197, "Not yet scheduled").

## Irreversibility

An npm version number is permanent: once published it can be deprecated, but
never republished with other bytes. A defect in this release is fixed by the
next one, which a new CLI release then pairs with.
